claims.text: Changing the percentages of Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr will alter the mechanical properties of HfNbTaTiZr.
The compositional effect on mechanical properties is caused by variations in lattice distortion and atomic interactions.
The initial alloy is an as-cast HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy.
The percentage of each of Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr will be varied systematically.
The alloys will be prepared by arc melting.
Arc melting will be followed by heat treatment at 1000°C for 24 hours.
Composition changes modify lattice distortion and atomic interactions among the constituent elements.
Changes in lattice distortion influence dislocation movement.
Changes in dislocation movement affect yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and ductility.
A 10% increase in Hf content will increase yield strength by 15% relative to the equiatomic baseline.
A 10% increase in Hf content will reduce ductility by 20% relative to the equiatomic baseline.
The baseline HfNbTaTiZr composition contains equal atomic percentages of all five elements.
Each constituent element will be restricted to a range of 10 to 30 atomic percent.
Compositions in the specified 10–30% range will remain single-phase solid solutions.
Processing conditions, impurities, and unaccounted interactions may cause variation in the measured mechanical properties.

contradictions.description: The prediction specifies a 15% yield-strength increase, but the falsification rule only rejects increases below 10%; outcomes from 10% to less than 15% would miss the stated prediction without falsifying it.
